en.headline: Customs arrests Tsim Sha Tsui salesman over untimely Chinese herb pricing
en.dek: Officers detained a 30-year-old local man after he revealed the total price only after grinding selected herbal medicines into powder.
body: Hong Kong Customs arrested a 30-year-old local salesman at a Tsim Sha Tsui medicine shop on Tuesday on suspicion of unfair trade practices involving a misleading omission.

According to Customs, during the sale of Chinese herbal medicines the salesman provided the total price only after the selected herbs had been ground into powder, an untimely disclosure that could mislead an average consumer into a transactional decision.

Customs said it maintains a Quick Response Team to handle urgent complaints from short-haul visitors and referred this case for priority investigation. The authority reminded traders to comply with the Trade Descriptions Ordinance and advised consumers to buy from reputable shops, check unit prices and confirm the total price before purchasing.
Under the ordinance, such practices can lead to a maximum fine of HK$500,000 and five years’ imprisonment upon conviction. An investigation is ongoing and the arrested man was held for inquiry.

zh.headline: 海關拘捕尖沙咀藥房店員 涉中藥材磨粉後才開價
zh.dek: 海關周二在尖沙咀一間藥房拘捕30歲本地男店員，指他在中藥材磨成粉末後才透露總價，涉嫌誤導性遺漏。
body: 香港海關周二在尖沙咀一間藥房拘捕一名30歲本地男店員，涉嫌在銷售中藥材過程中作出誤導性遺漏，違反《商品說明條例》。
海關表示，該店員在銷售中藥材時，以不適時的方式提供總價，即在有關中藥材被磨成粉末後，才向顧客透露其總價。此舉可能導致一般消費者作出交易決定。
海關指一直關注商戶以不良營商手法誤導旅客購物，並設有快速行動隊處理短期留港旅客的緊急投訴，會即時轉介調查人員優先處理。海關提醒商戶遵守條例規定，並建議市民光顧信譽良好商戶，留意計價單位，並在決定購買前查詢所選商品的總價格。
根據條例，有關行為一經定罪，最高可被罰款50萬元及監禁五年。案件仍在調查中，被捕人正接受查詢。
